If the user presses Ctrl+Z, the CompoundCommand undo removes that path and re-inserts the original element, but state.selectedPath and all the anchor/handle visuals still point at the now-detached path. Subsequent onMouseMove/onMouseUp do `state.selectedPath.setAttribute('d', ...)` on a node no longer in the document, and the commit `new ModifyAttributeCommand(state.selectedPath, 'd', newD)` records an edit against an orphaned element.
allFindings.impact: Convert-shape-to-path via direct-select then undo leaves the node editor operating on a ghost element: edits appear to do nothing, the undo stack gets a bogus ModifyAttributeCommand, and redo/undo can desync the history. Classic chained-failure: one feature (auto-convert) leaves state that breaks undo and later edits.
allFindings.fix: Subscribe to document/history changes and call deselect() when the selected path is removed, or re-resolve state.selectedPath from the document on each interaction instead of caching the node. At minimum, validate `state.selectedPath.isConnected` before setAttribute/commit.

allFindings.title: updatePathAnchor double-moves a control handle when an anchor is endpoint of one C and start of the next C
allFindings.evidence: In the second pass, for a C segment the code moves cp1 if `prevAnchorIdx === anchorIdx` and moves cp2 + endpoint if `currentIdx === anchorIdx`. For a smooth path `M.. C..a C..b` the shared anchor `a` is the endpoint of the first C (so its incoming cp2 moves) AND the start of the second C (so that segment's cp1 moves). That is correct for the two DISTINCT handles. BUT the delta dx/dy is computed once from oldPos, and `prevAnchorIdx`/`currentIdx` are advanced inside the C loop with `prevAnchorIdx = currentIdx; currentIdx++` per iteration — for a multi-pair C run (`C ... ...` with several triplets in one command) the SAME coords array is walked and a handle shared between two triplets in one command run can satisfy both conditions in adjacent iterations, applying dx twice to coords[i].
allFindings.impact: Dragging an anchor on a polybezier authored as a single multi-segment C command (e.g. `C c1 c2 p1 c3 c4 p2`) shifts a shared control handle by 2x the drag, kinking the curve. Wrong output on a common path shape.
allFindings.fix: Operate on a normalized one-triplet-per-C representation (parsePathD already does this), and explicitly track per-anchor incoming/outgoing handle indices rather than re-deriving from a shared coords array.

allFindings.title: joinPaths getLastPoint returns the M/start point when first path ends in Z, producing a bogus connector
allFindings.evidence: joinPaths computes `end1 = getLastPoint(cmds1)`. getLastPoint walks backward and returns the last command with points>0, but a Z command has `points: []`, so for a closed path `M..L..L..Z` it returns the last L point — fine. However after orientation, joinPaths does `if (final1[last].type === 'Z') final1 = final1.slice(0,-1)` to strip Z, then `connEnd = getLastPoint(final1)`. If reverseCommands was applied, reverseCommands DROPS the Z entirely (it only re-emits M/L/C), so a reversed closed path silently becomes open with no Z and a different endpoint than end1 used for the distance ranking.
allFindings.impact: Joining when one or both paths are closed can connect the wrong endpoints (ranking used pre-reverse endpoints that don't match post-reverse geometry) and/or silently un-close a closed shape. Wrong join result in the closed-path case.
allFindings.fix: Compute start/end consistently AFTER deciding orientation, and decide whether closed paths should even be join candidates; reverseCommands should preserve closure semantics or callers must account for its Z-dropping.

allFindings.title: Pen-tool double-click-to-finish also registers as a normal anchor click first
allFindings.evidence: onMouseDown checks double-click only at the very top: `if (state.drawing && anchors.length>=2 && lastClickPos) { ... if (dt<400 && dd<thresh){ finish(false); return } }`. But the FIRST click of a would-be double-click falls through to the `else` branch and runs `state.anchors.push(anchor); ...addAnchorVisual(...)`. So the sequence is: click adds anchor N, second click within 400ms/5px finishes. The added anchor N from the first click of the double remains in the path. Combined with the mouseup handler clearing handles only when drag<threshold, a fast double-click to end a path leaves an extra near-duplicate trailing anchor.
allFindings.impact: Finishing a path with a double-click frequently leaves a stray duplicate node at the end of the committed path. Minor geometry pollution; visible as a tiny zero-length segment and an extra editable node.
allFindings.fix: Detect the double-click before adding the anchor: if within time/dist of the previous anchor, treat as finish and do not push. Or pop the just-added anchor inside the double-click branch before finish().

allFindings.title: Node editor swallows nothing, but Delete/Backspace on a selected node is silently impossible (no handler) and falls through to whole-element delete
allFindings.evidence: directSelectTool defines `handlers: { onMouseDown, onMouseMove, onMouseUp }` with NO onKeyDown. Canvas.tsx dispatches keydown to `getActiveTool()?.handlers.onKeyDown?.(e)`. With a node selected (state.selectedAnchorIdx>=0) pressing Delete is not handled by the tool, so the global Delete (App.tsx 'Delete' context action deletes the whole selected ELEMENT). There is also no Escape/deselect-node handler.
allFindings.impact: A user in node-edit mode who selects a single anchor and presses Delete deletes the entire path, not the node — a surprising data-loss-shaped action. No way to delete an individual node at all. This is a real missing feature with a destructive fallback.
allFindings.fix: Add onKeyDown to directSelectTool handling Delete/Backspace (remove selected anchor, rebuild d via the structured parser, commit) and Escape (deselect node). preventDefault to stop the whole-element delete fallback.

allFindings.title: parsePathD negative-number split breaks scientific-notation exponents written with lowercase 'e' followed by sign in some forms, and the lookbehind requires modern engines
allFindings.evidence: `.replace(/(?<![eE])-/g, ' -')` splits on minus unless preceded by e/E. This relies on a lookbehind, fine for current targets, but the directSelect regex `[-\d.e+]+` (line 20/66/109/136) accepts e/+ but the subsequent `.split(/[\s,]+/).map(Number)` cannot recover a value like `1e-3` if the normalizer ever ran on it — the two parsers disagree on number grammar, compounding finding node-editing-1.
allFindings.impact: Edge-case number formats (exponential coordinates) parse differently between the two parsers, another way the node editor diverges from the rest of the app. Low because exponential coords are rare in this app's own output.
allFindings.fix: Unify on one parser (see node-editing-1) so number grammar is defined in exactly one place.

allFindings.title: splitCubicAt return type annotation lies (claims all four points are p0's type) and intersectLineWithPath Z uses first M, not subpath M
allFindings.evidence: In intersectLineWithPath the Z branch does `const mCmd = commands.find(c => c.type === 'M')` — always the FIRST M in the path. For a multi-subpath path (multiple M..Z groups), every Z incorrectly closes back to the very first subpath's start instead of its own subpath start.
allFindings.impact: Knife/intersection on a compound path (multiple subpaths, e.g. a donut or a letter 'O') computes wrong closing segments for all but the first subpath, yielding wrong or missing intersection points and bad cuts. Medium-ish but listed low because compound-path knifing may be rare in current usage.
allFindings.fix: Track the current subpath start (set on each M) and close Z to that, mirroring the curX/curY=startX/startY logic already present in parsePathD.

allFindings.title: simplifyPath can return duplicate-collapsed result that, combined with absolute-only assumption, is fine — but epsilon in screen vs doc units is unverified at call site
allFindings.evidence: pencilTool calls `simplifyPath(state.points, 0.5)` with a hardcoded 0.5. simplifyPath's epsilon is a perpendicular distance in whatever unit state.points is in (doc units after screenToDoc). 0.5 is a fixed doc-unit tolerance regardless of zoom/viewBox scale, unlike penTool/directSelect which scale thresholds by `vb.width/clientWidth`.
allFindings.impact: At high zoom the pencil over-simplifies (0.5 doc units may be many screen px); at low zoom it under-simplifies. Inconsistent with the rest of the subsystem which is zoom-aware. Cosmetic / UX, not corruption.
allFindings.fix: Scale the RDP epsilon by the current viewBox/client ratio like anchorDocSize/snapRadius do elsewhere.

allFindings.title: Text editing does not suppress global Ctrl shortcuts (undo/copy/paste/select-all fire mid-edit)
allFindings.evidence: EditorContext keydown guard: `if (isKeyboardCaptured() && !e.ctrlKey) return`. textTool sets keyboard capture during editing (textTool.ts:223) and its own onKeyDown explicitly bails on Ctrl combos (textTool.ts:404: `if (e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || e.metaKey) return`, except Ctrl+A). So while typing a text object, Ctrl+Z runs `history.undo()` (EditorContext.tsx:118) on a PRIOR document command, Ctrl+C/X/V/D operate on the document selection, and Ctrl+A both selects-all-text (textTool.ts:394) AND selects all document elements (EditorContext.tsx:157).
allFindings.impact: User typing text presses Ctrl+Z expecting to undo a typo and instead silently undoes a previously-committed shape; Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C/V behave wildly. Data-corruption-class confusion: the document mutates underneath an in-progress edit that itself isn't on the undo stack.
allFindings.fix: When keyboard is captured, suppress ALL editor bindings except a curated whitelist (or none) — e.g. `if (isKeyboardCaptured()) return` at top of EditorContext handler, and let the active tool own every key. Route Ctrl+A/C/V inside textTool to operate on its own buffer (Ctrl+A already does; add Ctrl+C/V/X for the text buffer or no-op them).

allFindings.title: Committed text uses font-size 16 in mm document space (~45pt giant glyphs)
allFindings.evidence: `const DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE = 16` (line 12) is written straight into the element: `'font-size': String(DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE)` (line 184). The document coordinate space is millimetres (coordinates.ts header: 'Convert screen (pixel) coordinates to document (mm) coordinates'; default artboard 210x297 = A4 mm in artboard.ts:41). A 16mm cap height is roughly 45pt.
allFindings.impact: Every text object created with the text tool is comically oversized for an A4 page; users must manually shrink font-size to ~3-4 every time. Caret/selection visuals (textTool.ts:99-100, DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE*0.8) inherit the same wrong scale.
allFindings.fix: Define the default in mm (e.g. ~3.5mm ≈ 10pt) or convert pt->mm at commit (pt * 25.4/72). Make the size configurable from defaultStyle so it matches the rest of the tool styling pipeline.

allFindings.title: Eraser multi-element undo can throw NotFoundError (insertBefore references a not-yet-restored sibling)
allFindings.evidence: On erase, each element records `nextSibling: hit.nextElementSibling` (lines 50, 65). On undo it iterates `elements` in erase order and does `pos.parent.insertBefore(el, pos.nextSibling)` (lines 104-112). If a drag erases two adjacent elements A and B where B was A's nextSibling, B is detached; restoring A first calls `insertBefore(A, B)` with B not in the DOM -> DOMException NotFoundError.
allFindings.impact: Erasing several overlapping/adjacent shapes in one drag, then Ctrl+Z, throws and aborts the undo (partial restore / broken history). Even when it doesn't throw, restoring in forward order against captured siblings can scramble z-order.
allFindings.fix: Restore in reverse erase order, and/or guard: if `pos.nextSibling` is detached (`!pos.parent.contains(pos.nextSibling)`) fall back to appendChild. Better: snapshot original child indices and reinsert by index after all removals are reverted.

allFindings.title: areaText.ts is dead code with incoherent mm/px units
allFindings.evidence: Grep shows `wrapText`/`buildAreaTextAttrs` are imported only by areaText.test.ts — never by any tool or component. wrapText signature is `(text, widthMm, fontSizePx)` and computes `charsPerLine = floor(widthMm / (fontSizePx * 0.6))` (lines 15-16), dividing a mm width by a px-named char width. buildAreaTextAttrs then emits `'font-size': String(fontSizePx)` (line 56) directly as an SVG attribute, which in this mm document is mm (same giant-font problem as draw-tools-2).
allFindings.impact: No user impact today (unwired), but it's a trap: any future wiring inherits broken unit math and oversized fonts. Carries maintenance + test weight for zero shipped value.
allFindings.fix: Delete the module (and its test) until area-text is actually built, or fix the unit model (single coordinate space) and wire it into a tool before keeping it.

allFindings.title: Lasso hit-test ignores ancestor (layer/group) transforms
allFindings.evidence: Lasso computes each candidate's bbox via `transformedAABB(child.getBBox(), child.getAttribute('transform'))` (lines 105-108). transformedAABB applies only the single passed transform (geometry.ts:18-19) — it does not compose the transform chain of ancestor `<g>`/layer elements. The lasso polygon is in document space (screenToDoc), so any transform above `child` puts the comparison in the wrong space.
allFindings.impact: Latent today (layer groups carry no transform), but recurs the documented leaf-vs-container transform fault. The moment a layer or wrapping group gains a transform (or grouped contents are lassoed via a transformed parent), selection silently selects the wrong elements.
allFindings.fix: Use a CTM-based AABB (compose getCTM relative to the SVG root, or screenToDoc the four screen-space bbox corners) instead of only the element's own transform attribute. Share one transform-aware AABB helper with hitTest.

allFindings.title: Text preview color hardcoded #000000, ignoring committed fill
allFindings.evidence: Preview text is created with `text.setAttribute('fill', '#000000')` (line 230) and caret stroke '#000000' (line 249), but commit() chooses `textFill = defaults.fill !== 'none' ? defaults.fill : defaults.stroke` (line 178). The on-screen preview can differ from the committed color.
allFindings.impact: WYSIWYG mismatch: user types in black, text commits in the current default color. Minor but jarring.
allFindings.fix: Compute textFill once and use it for both the preview element and the committed element.

allFindings.title: charOffset proportional fallback mispositions caret/selection for variable-width text
allFindings.evidence: When getSubStringLength is unavailable/throws, charOffset falls back to `totalLen * (pos / state.text.length)` (line 71) — linear interpolation assuming uniform char width. For proportional fonts the caret and the blue selection rect land at the wrong x.
allFindings.impact: Edge-case (only when getSubStringLength fails, e.g. some headless/test paths) caret and selection highlight drift from the actual glyph boundaries.
allFindings.fix: Acceptable as a degraded fallback, but gate selection-rect rendering on accurate measurement, or measure a real substring node. Low priority.

allFindings.title: Re-entrant commit() via onDeactivate -> setActiveTool('select')
allFindings.evidence: commit() calls `setActiveTool('select')` (line 196). registry.setActiveTool runs `prev?.onDeactivate?.()` BEFORE reassigning activeTool (registry.ts:36-40), and activeTool is still 'text' at that point, so text.onDeactivate -> commit() runs again re-entrantly. It's only saved by cleanup() having already set state.editing=false so the second commit returns early (line 266 guard).
allFindings.impact: Currently harmless but fragile: any future code path that re-enters before cleanup completes would double-commit or double-add the element.
allFindings.fix: Set a reentrancy/committing flag, or reorder so activeTool is reassigned before onDeactivate fires in the registry.

allFindings.title: Persisted measurement overlay relies on next tool's onDeactivate cleanup, lingers across re-entry
allFindings.evidence: onMouseUp intentionally leaves previewLine/previewText in the DOM ('Keep measurement visible until next interaction or tool switch', line 127). They are only removed by the next onMouseDown (removePreview at line 70) or onDeactivate (line 65). Tagged data-role='preview' so export strips them, but they persist in the live document tree between interactions.
allFindings.impact: Minor: stale pink measurement can remain visible; relies on deactivate firing. No data impact (stripped on save/export).
allFindings.fix: Acceptable design, but consider an explicit overlay layer for transient measurements rather than appending to the document SVG.

allFindings.title: Ctrl combos leak into document/history while editing text (chained-failure interlock)
allFindings.evidence: EditorContext: `if (isKeyboardCaptured() && !e.ctrlKey) return` — allows ALL Ctrl combos through during text editing. textTool.onKeyDown bails on every Ctrl combo: `if (e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || e.metaKey) return` (textTool.ts:404). startEditing() sets setKeyboardCapture(true) (textTool.ts:223). So while typing into a text object, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+X/Ctrl+V/Ctrl+C/Ctrl+D are handled by EditorContext against the document, not the text being typed.
allFindings.impact: User is mid-typing a text label; presses Ctrl+Z expecting to undo a typo and instead undoes the last DOCUMENT command (or pops history mid-edit). Ctrl+X deletes the previously-selected shape; Ctrl+V pastes shapes into the canvas; Ctrl+C copies the old selection. Classic 'state one feature left in a bad shape breaks the next' — text-edit capture is too coarse to protect the editor shortcuts.
allFindings.fix: While keyboardCaptured is true, EditorContext should suppress destructive editor shortcuts too (or text tool should consume Ctrl+C/X/V/Z/A and implement intra-text clipboard), not just single keys. Tighten the guard to a whitelist of editing-safe combos, or have textTool.onKeyDown e.preventDefault()/stopImmediatePropagation() for the combos it cannot service so they don't fall through to the sibling window listener.

allFindings.title: ToolConfig.icon is dead data in production — LeftRail hardcodes its own icons
allFindings.evidence: ToolConfig declares `icon: ReactNode` and every tool sets it (icon: 'V', 'R', 'T', ...). Grep for `.icon` in production: zero reads — only *.test.ts files assert `tool.icon`. LeftRail.tsx renders `<IconGlyph name={slot.key} .../>` from a hardcoded SLOTS array (key: 'select', 'directSelect', ...), never from the registry's icon field.
allFindings.impact: Every tool author maintains an icon the app never displays; tests pass while the real UI is wired elsewhere. Pure maintenance tax + false confidence from green tests.
allFindings.fix: Either make LeftRail render from getAllTools()/registry.icon (single source of truth) or drop the icon field from ToolConfig and the tools. Don't keep a tested-but-unused field.

allFindings.title: iconKeyForTool module is entirely dead code
allFindings.evidence: `export function iconKeyForTool(toolName)` is imported only by src/components/iconKeyForTool.test.ts — no production import anywhere (grep confirms). Its whole purpose (map registry tool names like 'direct-select'→'directSelect' for the ICONS dict) is duplicated inline by LeftRail's hardcoded SLOTS instead.
allFindings.impact: A whole adaptor module + its test exist solely to test themselves. Dead weight that misleads readers into thinking the registry feeds the icon system.
allFindings.fix: Delete the module and its test, OR actually route LeftRail's icon lookup through it so it earns its keep.

allFindings.title: LeftRail shortcut letters hardcoded separately from registry shortcuts — silent drift
allFindings.evidence: LeftRail SLOTS hardcode `{ key:'select', shortcut:'V', toolName:'select' }`, `{ key:'rect', shortcut:'R', toolName:'rectangle' }` etc., a second copy of the shortcut letters that registry tools already declare (selectTool shortcut:'v', rectTool shortcut:'r', ...). Nothing cross-checks the two. LeftRail even lists coming-soon shortcuts (B brush, K knife) that no registered tool owns.
allFindings.impact: If someone rebinds a tool's shortcut in its register*Tool file, the tooltip/badge in LeftRail still shows the old letter; or worse, two tools end up advertising the same key with no test catching it. findToolByShortcut would also resolve a duplicate to an arbitrary first-match (Array.from order).
allFindings.fix: Derive the displayed shortcut from the registry (getActiveTool/getAllTools) instead of a parallel literal table, and add a startup assertion that shortcuts are unique.

allFindings.title: GuidesState.reset() destroys subscribers and does not notify — asymmetric with DefaultStyleState
allFindings.evidence: reset(): `this.guides = []; this.nextId = 1; this.listeners = []` — it WIPES the listeners array and never calls notify(). Compare DefaultStyleState.reset() (defaultStyle.ts:42) which keeps listeners and fires them, and GuidesState.clearAll() (guides.ts:35) which keeps listeners and notifies. Currently only resetGuides() in tests calls it, but it's exported as a public API.
allFindings.impact: If reset() is ever called on a live state with mounted React subscribers (e.g. a future 'new document' / 'reset guides' menu action), every guides subscriber is silently orphaned — the Ruler/overlay stops updating forever with no error, and the UI won't even repaint to show the cleared guides. Latent footgun waiting for a caller.
allFindings.fix: Drop `this.listeners = []` from reset() and call this.notify() at the end, matching DefaultStyleState/clearAll semantics.

allFindings.title: Three uncoordinated window keydown listeners; preventDefault doesn't stop siblings
allFindings.evidence: window keydown listeners are registered independently in useToolShortcuts.ts:18, Canvas.tsx:360, and EditorContext.tsx:173. Each re-implements the same guards (INPUT/TEXTAREA tag check, isKeyboardCaptured()). useToolShortcuts calls e.preventDefault() (line 14) but that does NOT stop the other two window listeners from running for the same event — only stopImmediatePropagation would.
allFindings.impact: Guard logic is triplicated and already inconsistent (Canvas's tool-onKeyDown dispatch checks INPUT/TEXTAREA but NOT isKeyboardCaptured; the other two check both). Adding a new shortcut means remembering all three. A single key can be processed by multiple listeners; today the keyspaces happen not to collide, but there is no structural guarantee.
allFindings.fix: Introduce one central keyboard dispatcher that owns the window listener, applies the capture/tag guards once, and delegates to tool/editor handlers in a defined priority order. Remove the duplicated guards from the three sites.

allFindings.title: Document switch does not reset active tool or keyboard-capture flag
allFindings.evidence: setActiveDocument() swaps 9 active-state pointers (selection, layer, artboard, grid, guides, defaultStyle, smartGuides, wireframe, sourcePdf) but never touches the tool registry (activeTool / keyboardCaptured live as module globals in registry.ts and are not part of DocumentState).
allFindings.impact: If documents become switchable while a text edit is in progress, keyboardCaptured stays true across the swap and the textTool closure keeps a stale getSvg() reference to the old document — commit() could write the in-flight text into the wrong/old SVG, or the editor stays keyboard-locked with no visible caret. Speculative because multi-doc switching may not be user-reachable yet, but the omission is real.
allFindings.fix: On setActiveDocument(), force-commit/cancel any in-progress tool edit (e.g. getActiveTool()?.onDeactivate()) and reset keyboardCaptured, or make the active tool part of DocumentState.

allFindings.title: Markers rely on 'context-stroke' and are never emitted by the pdfExport engine
allFindings.evidence: Marker fills/strokes use `context-stroke` (markers.ts:59,72,85,99), a relatively young SVG2 value. The custom pdfExport engine (src/model/pdfExport.ts) has drawLine/drawPath but no marker-start/marker-end handling and no <defs>/<marker> walk — arrowheads added via PropertiesPanel.ensureMarkerDef won't appear in that export path.
allFindings.impact: Arrowheads render on-canvas but silently vanish in the pdf-lib export path (the production svg2pdf path may differ). Edge-case wrong output rather than corruption.
allFindings.fix: Either fall back to a concrete color when emitting markers for non-context-stroke consumers, or add marker resolution to the pdfExport walk; at minimum document that markers are export-path-dependent.

allFindings.title: registerTool silently overwrites on duplicate name; no uniqueness check on names or shortcuts
allFindings.evidence: registerTool just does `tools.set(config.name, config)` with no warning on collision, and there is no validation that shortcuts are unique across tools. findToolByShortcut returns the first Array order match for a duplicate.
allFindings.impact: A copy-paste bug giving two tools the same name or shortcut fails silently — one tool becomes unreachable with no diagnostic. Low because current registrations are clean.
allFindings.fix: Warn (or throw in dev) on duplicate name in registerTool, and add a dev-time assertion that shortcut letters are unique after registerAllTools().

allFindings.title: Gradient creation bypasses command history — undo desync + orphan-gradient leak
allFindings.evidence: const url = createLinearGradient(doc.getDefs(), colors?.color1 || '#000000', colors?.color2 || '#ffffff', 0)\napplyAttr(el, 'fill', url)   // only the fill attr is recorded in history; the <linearGradient> node was appended to <defs> directly by createLinearGradient/createRadialGradient with no Command
allFindings.impact: Switching fill-type to Linear/Radial appends a gradient straight into <defs> with no undo entry. Ctrl+Z reverts only the element's fill attribute, leaving the gradient stranded in the document; redo cannot recreate it if it had been removed. Toggling the fill-type select repeatedly (solid->linear->solid->linear) leaks a brand-new gradient every time because nothing reuses or GCs the previous one (no defs garbage collector exists — confirmed by grep). Over an editing session <defs> bloats with dead gradients that ship in the exported SVG/PDF.
allFindings.fix: Wrap gradient creation in a Command (e.g. an AddDefCommand whose execute appends the gradient and undo removes it) and execute it together with the fill ModifyAttributeCommand inside one CompoundCommand, so the whole fill-type switch is a single atomic undo step. Also reuse the existing gradient when toggling back instead of minting a new id each time.

allFindings.title: Setting rotation to 0 on a matrix-transformed element discards scale/translate (data loss)
allFindings.evidence: applyAttr(el, 'transform', angle === 0 && Math.abs(decomp.skewX) < 0.001 ? '' : matrixToString(newMat))
allFindings.impact: When an element carries a matrix() transform (e.g. produced by free-transform scaling) and the user types 0 into the R: field, the entire transform attribute is cleared to ''. Any non-identity scale or translate baked into that matrix is destroyed, so the element jumps/resizes. The guard only checks rotate==0 and skewX, ignoring decomp.scaleX/scaleY/translate. This is the classic 'matrix composition' fault-line.
allFindings.fix: Never blanket-clear the transform for matrix elements. Build the corrected matrix (rotation removed) and emit matrixToString(newMat); only emit '' when the recomposed matrix is genuinely the identity (all of scale==1, translate==0, skew==0, rotate==0).

allFindings.title: Gradient stop-color edits do not refresh the canvas overlay
allFindings.evidence: const cmd = new ModifyAttributeCommand(stops[0], 'stop-color', v)\nhistory.execute(cmd)   // no refreshOverlay(), unlike every other style edit which calls refreshOverlay()
allFindings.impact: Every other style/transform edit in this panel calls refreshOverlay() after history.execute, but the C1/C2 gradient color handlers (both stops) do not. If the selection overlay or any cached render derives from element bounds/appearance, the gradient recolor can leave stale overlay/handles until the next interaction. Inconsistent with the rest of the panel and a latent source of 'why didn't it update' bugs.
allFindings.fix: Call refreshOverlay() after history.execute in both gradient-stop onChange handlers, matching the convention used everywhere else in the file.

allFindings.title: Group (<g>) fill/stroke edit is a silent no-op when the group has no element children
allFindings.impact: Setting fill/stroke/stroke-width/opacity on a <g> distributes to children only. An empty group (or a group whose only descendants are nested deeper than one level) gets no change at all and the group's own attribute is never written, so the ColorPicker appears to do nothing. Distribution is also only one level deep — nested groups' leaf shapes are skipped, recreating the historical 'leaf-vs-container transform' fault-line for styling. opacity in particular is usually wanted on the group itself, not duplicated onto each child (which changes compositing semantics).
allFindings.fix: Recurse to leaf graphics elements rather than direct children, and for 'opacity' set it on the group itself. Fall back to setting the attribute on the group when there are no eligible children so the edit is never a silent no-op.

allFindings.title: Hex validation accepts 4- and 5-digit hex, producing invalid colors
allFindings.evidence: if (/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}$/.test(hex)) { onChange(hex) ... }
allFindings.impact: The regex {3,6} accepts 4- and 5-hex-digit strings (e.g. #abcd, #abcde) which are not valid CSS hex colors (only 3, 6, and with alpha 4/8 are). A user typing #abcd will have it accepted and written to the fill/stroke attribute, yielding an invalid color that renders as the SVG default (black) or is dropped on export.
allFindings.fix: Tighten to /^#([0-9a-fA-F]{3}|[0-9a-fA-F]{6})$/ (optionally add 4/8 if alpha hex is intended), and reject otherwise.

allFindings.title: Position inputs for path/g are permanently read-only no-ops in the Properties panel
allFindings.evidence: <PropertyInput label="X" value={String(aabb.x)} onChange={() => {}} />  // and Y/W/H all onChange={() => {}}
allFindings.impact: For path and g selections the panel shows editable-looking X/Y/W/H text inputs that silently discard any edit (empty onChange). Users will type a value, press Enter, and see it snap back with no feedback. The real path/g move logic lives only in ControlBar, so this is confusing duplicate, dead UI.
allFindings.fix: Either render these as plain read-only text (not <input>) for path/g, or wire them to the same translatePathD / computeTranslateAttrs logic the ControlBar uses.

allFindings.title: Gradient/textPath stop and startOffset edits write directly without numeric/format guard, and stops sit in <defs> where some validation assumptions break
allFindings.evidence: onChange={(v) => { const tp = el.querySelector('textPath'); if (tp) applyAttr(tp, 'startOffset', v) }}  // applyAttr's NUMERIC_ATTRS guard does not include startOffset, so '50%' or garbage both pass through
allFindings.impact: startOffset accepts arbitrary strings ('abc') and writes them, producing an invalid SVG attribute that breaks textPath rendering/export. Minor because textPath is a niche feature, but it is unvalidated user input flowing straight into the document.
allFindings.fix: Validate startOffset against a number-or-percentage pattern before applying, or add it to a percentage-aware validation set.

allFindings.title: getBBox()/transformedAABB fallback for text returns empty W/H, hiding W/H inputs and silently swallowing exceptions to 0,0,0,0
allFindings.evidence: } catch { return { x: '0', y: '0', w: '0', h: '0' } }  // any getBBox throw (detached node, display:none) silently reports the element at origin with zero size
allFindings.impact: If getBBox throws (element not laid out, hidden layer, just-created node), the control bar silently reports x=y=w=h=0. A user dragging the X/Y fields then computes deltas against a bogus 0 origin and can teleport the element to absolute 0,0. Edge case but a real coordinate-space trap.
allFindings.fix: Distinguish 'unavailable' from 'genuinely at 0' — return null/empty and disable the inputs when getBBox is unavailable rather than fabricating a 0,0 frame.

allFindings.title: Document Setup is a no-op: ArtboardDialog updates React state but never the artboard model Canvas reads
allFindings.evidence: ArtboardDialog onApply={setDimensions} only sets the `dimensions` React state. Canvas's effect `useEffect(() => { ... const bounds = computeDocumentBounds(); svgRef.current.setAttribute('viewBox', ...) }, [dimensions.width, dimensions.height])` recomputes the viewBox from `computeDocumentBounds()` which reads the unchanged artboard model. `updateArtboard()` exists in artboard.ts but is never called from the dialog (grep: ArtboardDialog only calls onApply).
allFindings.impact: Changing page size via File > Document Setup does nothing visible: the white artboard rect keeps its old size and the viewBox is re-set to the same old bounds. The displayed `dimensions` prop is also never used for the viewBox (computeDocumentBounds ignores it), so the prop and the model are permanently out of sync.
allFindings.fix: Have ArtboardDialog.onApply call updateArtboard(getActiveArtboard().id, {width,height}) (which notifies subscribers → syncArtboards re-renders the rect and triggers a bounds recompute), and drive the Canvas viewBox effect off the artboard model rather than the `dimensions` prop.

allFindings.title: Ruler drag-to-guide emits guides on the wrong coordinate axis
allFindings.evidence: HRuler handleMouseUp computes `const docX = viewBox.x + (px / canvasSize) * viewBox.width` then `addGuide('h', Math.round(docX * 10) / 10)`. A horizontal guide's `position` is a Y coordinate (Canvas.tsx renders 'h' guides as `y1=y2=guide.position`), but docX is an X value. VRuler is symmetrically wrong: it computes docY and calls `addGuide('v', docY)`, yet a 'v' guide's position is an X coordinate.
allFindings.impact: Dragging a guide off either ruler places it at a meaningless position (the orthogonal coordinate). Guides land far from where the user dropped them; the feature is effectively unusable.
allFindings.fix: HRuler should create a horizontal guide at the drop Y in doc space: compute docY from e.clientY relative to the canvas viewBox and call addGuide('h', docY). VRuler should compute docX from e.clientX and call addGuide('v', docX). This requires the ruler to know the canvas's screen rect / CTM, not just its own.

allFindings.title: Keyboard shortcuts fire while a <select> dropdown is focused (input guard misses SELECT and contentEditable)
allFindings.evidence: Global keydown guard is `const tag = (e.target as HTMLElement)?.tagName; if (tag === 'INPUT' || tag === 'TEXTAREA') return`. PropertiesPanel.tsx contains 7 `<select>` elements (fill type, stroke caps/joins, etc.). When a select is focused, tag === 'SELECT', so Delete/Backspace, arrow nudge, Ctrl+C/X/V/D/G all execute on the document selection. useToolShortcuts.ts has the same incomplete guard.
allFindings.impact: User opens a Properties dropdown, presses Backspace/Delete or an arrow to navigate options, and instead deletes/nudges the selected element. Ctrl+C/V also leak. This is a recurrence of the known 'inputs swallowing/leaking shortcuts' fault-line, on the other side (input leaking into editor).
allFindings.fix: Replace the tag check with a shared helper that also returns for tag === 'SELECT' and for `(e.target as HTMLElement)?.isContentEditable`. Use it in EditorContext, useToolShortcuts, and Canvas.

allFindings.title: Shift+Ctrl+' toggles grid visibility instead of grid snap (branch ordering / e.key collision)
allFindings.evidence: Visibility branch: `else if (e.ctrlKey && (e.key === "'" || e.key === '"') && !e.shiftKey)`. Snap branch (later): `else if (e.ctrlKey && (e.key === '"' || (e.key === "'" && e.shiftKey)))`. On most layouts Shift+' yields e.key === '"' AND e.shiftKey === true. The visibility branch's `!e.shiftKey` correctly excludes it, BUT the snap condition is reachable only if the prior branch is skipped — which it is. Re-reading: the real collision is the visibility branch accepts e.key === '"' even without intending shift; combined with the `!e.shiftKey` it is fine, however `toggleGridSnap` is gated behind a fragile e.key === '"' that depends entirely on keyboard layout and never on e.code, so on layouts where Shift+' does not produce '"' the snap shortcut is dead.
allFindings.impact: Grid snap toggle (Ctrl+Shift+') is layout-dependent and silently dead on many keyboards; grid visibility is the only reliably reachable toggle.
allFindings.fix: Disambiguate using e.code (e.g. 'Quote') plus e.shiftKey rather than e.key glyphs: visibility = Ctrl+Quote && !shift; snap = Ctrl+Quote && shift.

allFindings.title: Zoom emits cursorX/cursorY = 0, snapping the ruler cursor indicators to origin on every wheel tick
allFindings.evidence: emitState() always sends `cursorX: 0, cursorY: 0` (it has no pointer position), and it is called from the wheel handler (line 239). The mousemove handler sends the real doc cursor. So every zoom resets the ruler cursor triangles to viewBox origin until the next mousemove.
allFindings.impact: Ruler cursor indicators jump to 0,0 while zooming, and the StatusBar cursor readout flickers to 0,0. Cosmetic but visibly wrong during the common zoom-while-hovering interaction.
allFindings.fix: Track the last pointer client position in a ref and have emitState reuse it via screenToDoc, or have the wheel handler compute the doc cursor from e.clientX/Y like mousemove does.

allFindings.title: Selection overlay and selection state persist after switching to a drawing tool
allFindings.evidence: selectTool.onDeactivate clears drag/marquee state but never clears the selection set or overlay. EditorContext keydown (Delete, arrows, Ctrl+C/X/D/G) operates on getSelection() regardless of active tool. So with e.g. the Rect tool active, the previously-selected element stays highlighted and Delete/arrows still mutate it.
allFindings.impact: Pressing Delete while a drawing tool is active can delete a shape the user thinks is no longer 'active'. Defensible as an editor convention, but combined with the persistent overlay it is surprising.
allFindings.fix: Either (intentionally) keep selection but hide the transform overlay on non-select tools, or document/keep as-is. At minimum ensure the overlay handles are not shown while a creation tool is active.

allFindings.title: Canvas dispatches tool.onKeyDown for ALL keys including Ctrl combos already handled by EditorContext
allFindings.evidence: In the Canvas keydown effect: `if (tag !== 'INPUT' && tag !== 'TEXTAREA') { getActiveTool()?.handlers.onKeyDown?.(e) }` — no filtering of Ctrl/meta and no isKeyboardCaptured check. Both EditorContext and Canvas listen on window, so e.g. Ctrl+Z reaches the tool's onKeyDown AND EditorContext.undo. Today only textTool/penTool implement onKeyDown and they self-guard, so no live double-action, but the contract is fragile: any future tool that handles Escape/Enter/Arrows will collide with the global handlers and the firing order (child-effect Canvas listener registers before parent-effect EditorContext) is implicit.
allFindings.impact: Latent double-dispatch; a future tool reacting to a key the shell also handles will fire twice or fight over preventDefault.
allFindings.fix: Route all key handling through one dispatcher, or have Canvas skip dispatch when e.ctrlKey/metaKey and respect isKeyboardCaptured consistently with EditorContext.

allFindings.title: getSvgRef() is dead code and a competing source of truth for the SVG element
allFindings.evidence: `export function getSvgRef(): SVGSVGElement | null { const container = document.querySelector('[data-testid="canvas-container"]'); return container?.querySelector('svg') ?? null }`. grep finds zero callers outside Canvas.tsx. Meanwhile App keeps svgRef, EditorContext keeps docRef bound to a svg, and tools capture () => svgRef.current — three notions of 'the SVG'.
allFindings.impact: Maintenance hazard: a DOM-query-based accessor invites callers to bypass the ref plumbing and pick up a stale/wrong svg, especially under StrictMode remount. Currently just unused weight.
allFindings.fix: Delete getSvgRef, or if a global accessor is genuinely needed, have it return the same svgRef the rest of the system uses.

allFindings.title: Context-menu z-order and delete bypass the locked-layer / guard logic the menubar uses
allFindings.evidence: Context menu 'Bring to Front'/'Send to Back' build ReorderElementCommand inline, and 'Delete' builds RemoveElementCommand directly, with no check for locked layers; the menubar/Object menu routes through zOrder helpers and Ctrl+A explicitly skips data-locked='true' layers (EditorContext line 161-164). Two code paths for the same operations with divergent guards.
allFindings.impact: Right-click operations can move/delete elements on layers that Select-All deliberately excludes as locked, an inconsistency that will drift further as guards are added in only one path.
allFindings.fix: Make the context menu reuse the same zOrder/delete helpers as the menubar so guard logic lives in one place.

allFindings.title: ContextMenu can render off-screen near viewport edges
allFindings.evidence: Position is fixed at `left: x, top: y` straight from e.clientX/clientY with no clamping against window.innerWidth/innerHeight; minWidth 180.
allFindings.impact: Right-clicking near the right/bottom edge clips the menu; items can be unreachable.
allFindings.fix: After mount, measure the menu rect and shift left/up so it stays within the viewport.

allFindings.title: New bold/italic overlay text always renders as Carlito-Regular (multi-slot registry exists but is never populated)
allFindings.evidence: ensureFontIfNeeded registers exactly one Carlito slot: `const { fontkitFont: carlitoFont } = await registerCidFont(out, pageIdx, OVERLAY_FONT_KEY, opts.carlito)` then `slots.push({ key: OVERLAY_FONT_KEY, family: 'Carlito', weight: 'normal', style: 'normal', fontkitFont: carlitoFont })`. fileio.ts loads carlitoItalicUrl + carlitoBoldUrl but exportPdfBytes only passes `{ carlito }` (regular). So resolveFontKey('Arial','italic','bold') matches no family slot and returns fallbackKey = the normal-weight/normal-style Carlito.
allFindings.impact: Every user-authored bold or italic text run in a graft/mixed export renders in upright regular weight. The makeFontRegistry multi-slot routing (graftExport.fontRegistry.test.ts) is fully built and tested but receives only one slot in production. Source-text edits keep their original face (gatherSourceFontSlots), so this only bites NEW text — but that is the common 'add a bold heading' case.
allFindings.fix: Thread carlitoBold + carlitoItalic (and bold-italic) through ExportViaGraftOpts and register them as additional slots in ensureFontIfNeeded with weight/style set to bold/italic, keyed e.g. VfCarlitoBold/VfCarlitoItalic. fileio.ts already fetches the bytes.

allFindings.title: Layer's own transform is dropped on the overlay/non-foundation walk path
allFindings.evidence: walkLayer(layer, ctx, ops, registry) iterates `Array.from(layer.children)` and calls walkOne on each child; walkOne reads only the CHILD's transform attribute. The layer (`g[data-layer-name]`) element's own `transform` attr is never composed into ctx. Contrast emitElementWithAncestors (line 312) which walks `cur !== layer.parentElement`, INCLUDING the layer node, so the mixed-foundation path DOES apply the layer transform. The two code paths disagree.
allFindings.impact: A layer group carrying a transform (e.g. imported nested PDF layer, or any future per-layer transform) has its overlay/new content emitted at the wrong position in overlay and non-foundation cases, while the same content under the mixed-foundation path would be placed correctly. Inconsistent, position-shifting export.
allFindings.fix: Seed walkLayer's context with the layer's own transform: compose parseTransform(layer.getAttribute('transform')) into ctx before iterating children, mirroring emitElementWithAncestors' inclusion of the layer node.

allFindings.title: Group-inherited fill/stroke/opacity is silently dropped — leaves only read their own attributes
allFindings.evidence: Every emitter resolves paint from the element alone: emitRect does `parseColor(el.getAttribute('fill'))` / `parseColor(el.getAttribute('stroke'))` with no ancestor inheritance walk. walkOne composes transforms but never fill/stroke/opacity. PropertiesPanel.tsx:130 lets the user set fill/stroke/stroke-width/opacity on a `<g>`, and line 673-674 exposes an `opacity` editor; the canvas renders these via SVG inheritance.
allFindings.impact: A `<g fill="#ff0000">` wrapping fill-less children renders red on the canvas but exports with no fill (invisible / black per default). PropertiesPanel mitigates by distributing group fill to DIRECT children only (CompoundCommand at :131), so single-level groups survive, but nested groups and any opacity/fill-opacity are lost. Canvas-vs-export mismatch.
allFindings.fix: Either inherit fill/stroke/opacity down the ancestor chain in the emitters (preferred, matches SVG semantics), or document the limitation and have PropertiesPanel recurse group style to all descendant leaves. Opacity (constant-alpha gs / fill-opacity) needs separate op emission.

allFindings.title: Rotated/skewed text loses its rotation — Tm emits pure translation despite per-point rotation for shapes
allFindings.evidence: emitText emits `1 0 0 1 ${fmt(run.pos.x)} ${fmt(run.pos.y)} Tm` — an identity-rotation text matrix; only the translated baseline (run.pos, which is matrix-applied + Y-flipped) carries any transform. The module header (lines 16-19) claims per-point transform 'so that rotation in the matrix is honoured (rect/ellipse/etc rotate correctly)'. Text is silently exempt from that guarantee.
allFindings.impact: Any text under a rotation or skew transform exports upright at the (correctly placed) origin instead of rotated. Matches legacy pdfExport's limitation (not a regression) but the header doc is misleading and the output is wrong for rotated labels/callouts.
allFindings.fix: Build the Tm from the composed matrix's a/b/c/d (with the Y-flip sign-corrected) instead of `1 0 0 1`, or at minimum amend the header comment to exclude text from the rotation guarantee.

allFindings.title: All coordinate emission assumes MediaBox origin at (0,0); non-zero-origin source pages misplace overlays and redactions
allFindings.evidence: pageHeightPtOf returns `mb.get(3).asNumber() - mb.get(1).asNumber()` (height only — origin discarded). svgMmToPdfPt (graftCs.ts:94) computes `ctx.pageHeightPt - t.y*MM_TO_PT` with no x/y MediaBox offset, and applyRedactionsToPage (graftMupdf.ts:255-261) uses `pageHeightPt = bounds[3]-bounds[1]` and setRect([r.x, ...]) without adding bounds[0]/bounds[1].
allFindings.impact: For a source PDF whose page 0 MediaBox has a non-zero lower-left origin (legal and not rare), every emitted overlay primitive and every redaction rect is offset by (-x0, -y0), shifting modifications/new content and mis-targeting text excision. Output silently misregistered.
allFindings.fix: Carry the MediaBox lower-left (x0,y0) into Ctx and add it in svgMmToPdfPt and the redaction rect construction; or normalize the grafted page's MediaBox to origin (0,0) after grafting.

allFindings.title: Second mixed layer from the same source: its deletions are never redacted and it re-renders lossily
allFindings.evidence: Redaction only runs for the foundation: `if (foundIdx !== -1 && classifications[foundIdx].cls.kind === 'mixed')`. emitLayerOverlay routes any NON-foundation mixed layer to walkLayer (line 256-263), which renders the whole layer as overlay and ignores cls.removedBboxes / cls.modifiedElements entirely.
allFindings.impact: If a document has two layers tagged to the same primary source (foundation graft/mixed + a second mixed layer), deletions on the second layer are not excised from the (shared) grafted source bytes, so 'deleted' source text/shapes remain in the export and stay Ctrl+F-findable. The single-layer primary import path (PRIMARY_LAYER_ID) avoids this today, making it latent rather than always-live.
allFindings.fix: Accumulate redact rects from ALL graft/mixed layers whose sourceEntry matches the grafted foundation source, not just the foundation, before applyRedactionsToPage. Long-term: the multi-graft-per-page work the comments reference.

allFindings.title: Non-#hex / non-black/white colors (rgb(), rgba 8-digit hex, named) parse to null → element silently invisible
allFindings.evidence: parseColor only handles #rgb, #rrggbb, 'black', 'white'; everything else returns null. emitRect/emitEllipseLike/emitPath then hit `if (!fill && !stroke) return ''` and emit nothing. lassoTool uses 'rgba(37,99,235,0.08)' (preview only), but any future rgb()/named/8-digit-alpha fill on a persisted shape exports invisibly.
allFindings.impact: Today the editor writes #rrggbb fills so this rarely bites, but a color value the parser doesn't recognize makes the whole shape vanish from the PDF with no warning rather than degrading gracefully.
allFindings.fix: Extend parseColor to handle rgb()/rgba() and the standard named-color set (or at least fall back to black with a console warn instead of dropping the element).

allFindings.title: NaN geometry attributes pass the <=0 guard and emit degenerate ops
allFindings.evidence: num() returns parseFloat(v) which can be NaN. emitRect: `if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return ''` — `NaN <= 0` is false, so a width="abc" proceeds; fmt(NaN) returns '0' (line 53), producing a zero-size or malformed path body rather than skipping the element.
allFindings.impact: Malformed/empty attribute values produce silent degenerate geometry instead of being skipped. Robustness only; current tools always write valid numbers.
allFindings.fix: Guard with `!Number.isFinite(w) || w <= 0` (and same for other dimensions) so non-finite inputs short-circuit to ''.

allFindings.title: Whitespace-only text not filtered despite emitText doc claiming 'returns "" for empty/all-whitespace'
allFindings.evidence: collectTextRuns plain-text branch: `const text = el.textContent ?? ''; if (!text) return []`. A run of spaces ('   ') is truthy, so it proceeds and shapes spaces. The emitText docstring (line 437) states 'Returns "" for empty/all-whitespace content.'
allFindings.impact: Cosmetic: empty space-only text elements still emit a BT/Tf/Tm/TJ block. No visual artifact, but the doc contract is false and it bloats the stream slightly (works against the determinism/golden goals).
allFindings.fix: Trim-check: treat content as empty when text.trim() === '' for whitespace-only runs, or fix the docstring to match actual behavior.

allFindings.title: Source font registered but unreferenced when coverage fallback routes all its runs to Carlito (orphan resource)
allFindings.evidence: gatherSourceFontSlots registers a CID font on the page for EVERY unique matched source font of modified text. emitText (graftCs.ts:450-456) may then reassign run.fontKey to the Carlito fallback when fontCoversText fails, so no content stream ever references the registered source key. subsetFonts() then runs over an orphan font entry.
allFindings.impact: Wasted embedding/registration work and a font key in /Resources/Font that no stream uses; subsetFonts must prune it. No corruption, just inefficiency and a slightly larger pre-subset doc. Cuts against the byte-determinism story if pruning isn't fully deterministic.
allFindings.fix: Register source fonts lazily on first actual emit, or post-pass and remove font resources with zero references before subsetFonts.

allFindings.title: Deleting a background-PDF layer never removes its bytes/source-entry from SourcePdfStore
allFindings.evidence: deleteLayer(): `const cmd = new RemoveElementCommand(editor.doc, layers[idx].element); editor.history.execute(cmd)` — no call to store.removeBackground(layerName). SourcePdfStore.removeBackground() (sourcePdf.ts:42) exists but is never called from any production file (grep: only the import path mutates the store).
allFindings.impact: After importing a background PDF and deleting its layer, the original ~10MB PDF bytes stay pinned in the store for the document's lifetime (memory leak). Worse, the orphaned background entry still keys by the old layer name; re-importing a PDF whose name sanitizes to the same key, or re-adding a layer with that data-src-layer-id, makes the graft engine clone content from the wrong/deleted source. Undo of the delete also won't re-tie state correctly.
allFindings.fix: When a layer with a data-src-layer-id is removed (and on undo/redo of that command), call store.removeBackground(layerId) / re-add on undo. Best done inside RemoveElementCommand or a layer-lifecycle hook so it survives undo/redo, not in the React handler.

allFindings.title: Open SVG / New Document leave stale SourcePdfStore.primary set
allFindings.evidence: applyParsedSvg() (fileio.ts) clears layers and defs but never touches the SourcePdfStore. SourcePdfStore.reset()/clearPrimary() are defined (sourcePdf.ts:34,61) but never called in production (grep confirms). Only recordImportedSource('primary') → clearAll() ever clears it.
allFindings.impact: Sequence: Open PDF (sets store.primary + ~10MB bytes) → Open SVG → store.primary still references the discarded PDF. Today this is masked because the freshly-imported SVG layers carry no data-src tags so classifyLayer returns 'overlay' and exportPdf falls back to pdf-lib (fileio.ts:188-199). But the bytes leak, and the routing is one stray data-src attribute away from grafting from a document that no longer exists. The store's own doc-comment claims 'a fresh primary import replaces the whole document' — Open SVG is also a whole-document replace and is not covered.
allFindings.fix: Call getActiveSourcePdfStore().reset() inside applyParsedSvg (fileio.ts) and on New Document, mirroring the clearSelection() already done there.

allFindings.title: pdf-lib fallback drops rotation, skew, and non-uniform shear on every non-text element
allFindings.evidence: extractScale() returns only sx=√(a²+b²), sy=√(c²+d²) and drawRect/drawEllipseEl/drawCircleEl/drawImage size/position purely via this scale + svgPtToPdf of one corner. The header comment even admits: 'For rotation-only transforms returns {1, 1}.' A parent <g transform="rotate(...)"> or a MuPDF leaf transform with rotation is silently flattened to an axis-aligned box.
allFindings.impact: Any rotated rect/ellipse/circle/image in the document exports unrotated and mis-placed via the pdf-lib path (background composites, freshly authored docs). drawPath is fine (full matrix applied to every point); the primitives are not. Word/Designer PDFs with rotated logos/photos export wrong.
allFindings.fix: Either route primitives through full-matrix path emission (convert rect/ellipse to a path and use transformPathD), or pass the affine to pdf-lib via a content-stream cm operator / drawImage's rotate option instead of pre-extracting a scalar scale.

allFindings.title: Bold serif and italic+bold combinations collapse to the wrong weight
allFindings.evidence: pickFont(): `if (isSerif && italic) return fonts.serifItalic; if (isSerif) return fonts.serifRegular; if (italic) return fonts.sansItalic; if (bold) return fonts.sansBold;`. There is no serifBold slot and bold is only checked AFTER italic for sans, so bold-serif → serifRegular (no bold), and bold+italic sans → sansItalic (no bold).
allFindings.impact: Headings in serif Word/designer PDFs (Playfair/Times bold) export as regular weight; bold-italic runs lose bold. Visible weight regression on round-trip, which is the exact class of defect this engine was built to fix.
allFindings.fix: Add serifBold/serifBoldItalic font slots, and combine style+weight: pick by (serif?, bold?, italic?) over the full 2×2×2 matrix rather than early-returning on the first match.

allFindings.title: parseColor handles only #hex/black/white — every named color and rgb()/hsl() exports as no-fill or black
allFindings.evidence: parseColor only matches #rgb, #rrggbb, 'black', 'white'; everything else returns undefined. In drawText, `color: fill ?? rgb(0,0,0)` turns an unrecognized fill into black; in drawRect/drawPath an unrecognized fill becomes no-fill (invisible).
allFindings.impact: SVG content using named colors (red, currentColor), rgb()/rgba(), or hsl() — all common — exports with wrong/invisible fills via the pdf-lib path. MuPDF emits hex so imported-PDF round-trips are mostly safe, but user-authored shapes are not.
allFindings.fix: Use a real CSS color parser (or at least add the SVG named-color table, rgb()/rgba(), and percentage forms). Distinguish 'unparseable' from 'none' so text doesn't silently become black.

allFindings.title: Two background imports whose names share a 40-char prefix overwrite each other's source bytes
allFindings.evidence: sanitizeLayerNameFromFile clamps to 37 chars + '...' (pdfImport.ts:224). applyParsedAsBackgroundLayer tags the layer with layerId=layerName AND recordImportedSource('background', layerName) keys the map by the same clamped string. Two distinct files with identical first 37 chars produce the same key → store.backgrounds.set overwrites.
allFindings.impact: The first background's bytes are silently replaced; both layers' data-src-layer-id now resolve to the second PDF, so graft export clones the wrong source for one of them. Edge case but data-corrupting when hit.
allFindings.fix: Decouple the store key from the display name: use a generated unique id (counter/uuid) for data-src-layer-id and the map key; keep the clamped name only as the human-readable data-layer-name.

allFindings.title: Shipped console.log/console.warn debug spam in drawImage hot path
allFindings.evidence: drawImage: `console.log('[pdfExport] drawImage', {...})` (line 302) and `console.log('[pdfExport] drawImage emit', {...})` (line 319), plus a console.warn on embed failure. Matches the WIP commit df591f5 'drawImage debug logs'.
allFindings.impact: Every image logs twice per export to the user console; leaks document detail and noise. Not a correctness bug but staff-review-blocking for a shipped path.
allFindings.fix: Remove the console.log lines (keep the embed-failure warn, or gate all behind a debug flag).

allFindings.title: Per-character drawText with subset:false embeds full fonts and issues one PDF text op per glyph
allFindings.evidence: drawText per-char path loops `for (i of chars) drawTextRun(chars[i], ...)` (one drawText op per glyph), and embedFonts deliberately uses `embedFont(bytes, { subset: false })` (pdfExport.ts:517) embedding the entire TTF. safeEncode also calls font.encodeText twice on the happy path region.
allFindings.impact: Large MuPDF-imported PDFs (per-char tspans for ~40% of runs per the comment) produce bloated content streams and a multi-MB embedded font per family, with O(glyphs) op overhead. Acceptable for MVP, costly at scale; export of a long document can be slow and produce large files.
allFindings.fix: Subset fonts once at save time (pdf-lib subset machinery, or collect used codepoints and subset), and coalesce consecutive per-char runs that share x-advance into single TJ runs where positions are monotonic.

allFindings.title: postProcessPdfSvg viewBox-to-mm regex replaces only the first match and assumes a single page
allFindings.evidence: s.replace(/viewBox="..."/, ...) without the /g flag converts only the first viewBox. The whole pipeline also hard-codes pageIndex=0 (renderPageToSvg default; importPdf never passes another page) while plumbing pageCount through — so multi-page PDFs import only page 1 with no UI affordance for the rest.
allFindings.impact: Nested/multiple viewBox attributes (rare in MuPDF output) would be left in pt. More importantly, multi-page PDFs silently import only the first page despite pageCount being tracked — a feature gap users will hit.
allFindings.fix: Add /g (or anchor to the root svg) for the viewBox replace; expose page selection (the worker already accepts pageIndex and returns pageCount).

allFindings.title: removeBackground/clearPrimary/reset are dead code, signalling the cleanup contract was never wired
allFindings.evidence: grep across src (excluding tests) shows clearPrimary (sourcePdf.ts:34), removeBackground (:42), and reset (:61) have zero production callers. Only recordImportedSource→clearAll and the import/add paths run.
allFindings.impact: The store has a full lifecycle API but only the 'add' half is connected — the dead removers are the root signature of findings pdf-io-1 and pdf-io-2 (no teardown path exists).
allFindings.fix: Wire these into layer-delete (removeBackground), Open SVG / New Document (reset), and primary re-open (already via clearAll); or delete them if a different teardown is chosen — but the gap itself is the bug.

allFindings.title: Dead deletion-detection API + junk attribute leaked into saved SVG
allFindings.evidence: layer.setAttribute(SOURCE_COUNT_ATTR, String(count)) // 'data-vf-source-count'. expectedSourceCount() and currentSourceCount() are the only consumers of this attr, and grep shows they have ZERO production callers — classifyLayer uses findRemovedElementBboxes for removal detection, not the counts.
allFindings.impact: Every imported source layer gets data-vf-source-count stamped on it. exportSvgString() does not strip data-* and serializes it verbatim, so saved/exported SVGs carry meaningless editor metadata. The count-based removal API it was meant to support is entirely dead — confusing surface area and a latent two-source-of-truth bug if someone wires it up alongside the bbox path.
allFindings.fix: Delete expectedSourceCount, currentSourceCount, SOURCE_COUNT_ATTR, the setAttribute call, and the count local — removal detection already lives in findRemovedElementBboxes. If the attribute must stay, strip it in exportSvgString alongside the overlay scrub.

allFindings.title: Moving a source element to another layer is misreported as a deletion (false mask)
allFindings.evidence: for (const [, snap] of registry) { const el = snap.weakRef.deref(); if (!el || !layer.contains(el)) { removed.push(snap.bboxMm) } }
allFindings.impact: Removal is judged purely by 'is this element still inside THIS layer'. If the user drags a source element into a different layer (a normal operation), layer.contains(el) is false even though the element is alive and visible. The graft engine then paints a white mask rect over its original location while the element renders at its new spot — on export the content is whited-out/duplicated. Same false positive if reparented under a <g> the walk misses. The element-still-alive deref check is computed but the cross-layer case is not distinguished from true deletion.
allFindings.fix: Distinguish 'gone from DOM entirely' from 'moved elsewhere in the doc'. Check el.isConnected / document.contains(el) before treating as removed; only mask when the element is truly gone from the rendered tree.

allFindings.title: Documented 'text content tracked at Command level' contract is unwired (commandTouchesSource consumed nowhere)
allFindings.evidence: Doc comment: 'Text content changes are tracked at the Command level (see Command.touchesSource)'. But grep shows commandTouchesSource / .touchesSource() is referenced ONLY inside commands.ts and this comment — no export/classify code calls it. isElementModified compares attributes only (currentAttrs vs snap), never textContent.
allFindings.impact: isElementModified is attribute-only by design and explicitly defers text-content edits to a Command signal that is never read. There is also no text-content edit command in commands.ts (textTool only ADDS new overlay text). The contract is fiction. When Phase-3 in-place source-text editing lands (mutating an existing source <text>'s textContent without changing attributes), isElementModified returns false, findModifiedSourceElements omits it, classifyLayer returns 'graft', and export grafts the PRISTINE source bytes — the user's text edit is silently lost on PDF export.
allFindings.fix: Either wire commandTouchesSource into the modified set used by classifyLayer, or have isElementModified also compare a captured textContent hash for text/tspan. Until in-place editing exists, at minimum fix the doc comment so it doesn't claim a guarantee the code doesn't provide.

allFindings.title: Snapshot baseline is in-memory-only and never rebuilt on SVG reload
allFindings.evidence: const snapshots: WeakMap<Element, Map<string,string>> = new WeakMap(); layerSnapRegistry: WeakMap<Element, Map<string, ElementSnap>>. snapshotImportedElements is called ONLY from pdfImport.ts (lines 291, 338) — never from the .svg load path in fileio.ts.
allFindings.impact: data-src-* and data-source-pdf-id survive serialization into a saved .svg, but the snapshot baseline does not. Reopen a saved doc with source-tagged layers and the snapshot WeakMap is empty, so isElementModified/findModifiedSourceElements report NOTHING modified for genuinely-edited content. Currently masked only because SourcePdfStore (store.primary) is also session-scoped so shouldUseGraftEngine returns false on a fresh reload and routes to pdf-lib. Fragile coupling: if source-PDF bytes ever get persisted/restored without also rebuilding snapshots, edits silently revert to pristine source on export.
allFindings.fix: Make the snapshot baseline reconstructable from serialized state (persist a per-element baseline, or re-snapshot on load whenever a layer carries data-source-pdf-id), and assert in classifyLayer that a source layer with a live store also has a snapshot baseline (fail loud rather than silently grafting pristine).

allFindings.title: matchSvgFontToSource / extractEmbeddedFontBytes hardcode page index 0, ignoring data-src-page
allFindings.evidence: const match = matchSvgFontToSource(el, src, 0); ... const extracted = extractEmbeddedFontBytes(src, 0, match.fontKey) — page index is the literal 0, while sourceTagging stamps a real page via data-src-page (getSourceMeta(el).page).
allFindings.impact: Today every PDF import uses {page:0} (pdfImport.ts), so this is latent. But the tagging layer records the true source page and listPageFonts/extractEmbeddedFontBytes take a pageIdx parameter — once multi-page import lands, font extraction reads fonts from the wrong page (or fontKey won't exist on page 0), so source-font preservation for edited text on pages >0 silently falls back to Carlito with wrong metrics. The core promise of the subsystem (seamless in-place edits) breaks.
allFindings.fix: Derive the page from getSourceMeta(el).page instead of hardcoding 0, in both the match and extract calls in gatherSourceFontSlots.

allFindings.title: pageKey derived from baseFont can collide across distinct source fonts
allFindings.evidence: const pageKey = `VfSrc${extracted.baseFont.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '_')}`. Dedup upstream is by match.fontKey (seenFontKeys), NOT by pageKey.
allFindings.impact: Two different source font keys whose BaseFont names sanitize to the same string would map to the same page-resource key. registerCidFont gets called twice with the same pageKey, the second overwriting the first's page resource, so one run of text shapes against the wrong glyph program. Narrow in practice (subset prefixes usually differ) but the dedup key and the resource key being different invariants is a smell.
allFindings.fix: Dedup and key on the same identity: include the fontKey (or a hash of the program bytes) in pageKey, or skip when pageKey is already registered.

allFindings.title: parseFontSuffix maps 'heavyitalic' to weight=bold (wrong cut)
allFindings.evidence: if (s === 'bolditalic' || s === 'boldoblique' || s === 'heavyitalic') { return { weight: 'bold', style: 'italic' } }
allFindings.impact: Heavy (~900) is collapsed to bold (700). For exact-triple matching this is harmless because matchSvgFontToSource falls back to family+style, but it produces a misleading parsed weight and is inconsistent with the s.includes('italic') branch below which would otherwise preserve 'heavy'. Cosmetic / future-correctness only.
allFindings.fix: Drop 'heavyitalic' from the bold-italic branch and let the generic s.includes('italic') handler return weight='heavy', style='italic'.

allFindings.title: tagImportedLayer recurses into already-tagged <text>, tagging child <tspan> independently
allFindings.evidence: if (TAGGABLE_TAGS.has(tag)) { setAttribute(SRC_PAGE/LAYER) }  // 'text' AND 'tspan' both taggable; then: if (child.children.length > 0) walkAndTag(child, meta) — so a <text> gets tagged and then its <tspan> children also get tagged.
allFindings.impact: Each tspan independently carries data-src-* and gets its own snapshot. Combined with snap-3 (attribute-only diff) a tspan whose text is edited but whose attrs are unchanged is invisible to modification detection at BOTH levels. It also inflates the (dead) SOURCE_COUNT and the registry with one entry per tspan, double-counting if count-based logic is ever revived. Not harmful today but couples awkwardly with the dead count path and the missing text-content diff.
allFindings.fix: Either tag only the outermost text-bearing element (don't recurse into <text>), or make the diff logic tspan-text-aware so the redundant tagging actually buys correctness.

allFindings.title: decomposeMatrix returns wrong scaleY and a non-SVG skewX when the matrix contains shear
allFindings.evidence: const scaleY = Math.sqrt(c * c + d * d) ... const skewX = Math.atan2(a * c + b * d, a * d - b * c) * (180 / Math.PI)  — for a pure skewX(30) (matrix [1,0,tan30,1,0,0]) this yields scaleY=1.1547 instead of 1.0 (verified numerically). A correct QR/Gram-Schmidt decomposition divides scaleY by cos(skew): scaleY = det/scaleX, and skew = atan2(a*c+b*d, scaleX*scaleX).
allFindings.impact: Any shape carrying a matrix() transform with shear (PDF/SVG imports, free-transform output) shows incorrect Scale-Y and Skew-X numbers in the Properties panel, and ControlBar's matrix() rotation-replace branch (line 260-266) reads decomp.skewX to decide whether to blank the transform, so a sheared element can be mis-detected. Rotate output is correct, which is why this hasn't surfaced loudly.

allFindings.title: Rotate-center regex in the rect/ellipse branch omits exponent chars, inconsistent with the path branch
allFindings.evidence: Line 113 uses match(/rotate\(([-\d.]+)(?:,\s*([-\d.]+),\s*([-\d.]+))?\)/) while the path branch at line 85 uses the exponent-aware /rotate\(([-\d.e+-]+)...)/. The same narrow pattern is duplicated in selectTool.ts:243 and ControlBar.tsx:55/408 and PropertiesPanel.tsx:408.
allFindings.impact: If a rotate center was ever serialized in exponential form (e.g. 1e-7 from a matrix round-trip), translating a rotated rect/ellipse/circle/text silently fails to shift the rotation pivot, so the shape pivots around a stale point after a move. Narrow trigger, but a latent correctness landmine because two branches in the SAME function disagree.

allFindings.title: computeSmartGuides emits guide lines via a 0.01 hard-coded re-scan that can drop or duplicate lines
allFindings.evidence: After choosing bestDx, it re-loops xCandidates and pushes a guide for every v with Math.abs(snappedEdge - v) < 0.01. The snap delta bestDx is computed in float mm and snappedEdge = edge + bestDx; rounding can make the matched candidate fall just outside 0.01 (no line drawn despite a snap), or multiple candidates within 0.01 produce duplicate guides (renderGuides dedups by value.toFixed(2), but the recompute work is wasted). Tie-breaking in the snap search (dist < bestDistX) also silently prefers the last-seen candidate.
allFindings.impact: Occasionally the magenta alignment line does not appear even though the element snapped, or flickers. Cosmetic only; the snap correction (dx/dy) itself is correct.

allFindings.title: snapToGrid always snaps to minorSpacing and snaps the cursor, not element edges
allFindings.evidence: snap() does Math.round(x / s) * s with s = minorSpacing. selectTool.ts:562 calls snapToGrid(pt.x, pt.y) on the raw pointer, so the delta dx = snapped.x - dragState.startX snaps the CURSOR to grid, not the element's bbox edges. majorSpacing is never used for snapping.
allFindings.impact: Snap-to-grid does not align element edges to grid lines (the canonical expectation); it aligns the grab point. An element grabbed off-center never lands flush on a gridline, which reads as 'grid snap is broken'. Also grid-snap and smart-guides both run in the same drag frame (selectTool 562 then 574), so they can fight and produce a jittery net delta.

allFindings.title: parseTransform and parseSkew silently produce NaN matrices on malformed input
allFindings.evidence: args = match[2].split(/[\s,]+/).map(Number); a translate() with a non-numeric or empty arg yields NaN, multiplied into the result with no guard. matrix() with fewer than 6 args puts undefined→NaN into slots. parseSkew's /skewX\(([-\d.]+)\)/ also won't match exponent or '+'-signed values.
allFindings.impact: A single malformed transform attribute (hand-edited SVG, exotic import) silently turns an element's matrix into NaN, which then poisons every transformedAABB / hit-test / align computation that touches it (NaN comparisons are all false, so the element becomes unselectable/unhittable). No crash, just a vanishing element. Defensive Number.isFinite guards would localize the failure.

allFindings.title: ArtboardState.layout is hard-coded to a single horizontal row at y=0
allFindings.evidence: layout(): let x = 0; for (const ab of this.artboards) { ab.x = x; ab.y = 0; x += ab.width + GAP }. bounds() and atPoint() are written generically (minY/maxY) but layout can never produce a non-zero y, so the generality is dead.
allFindings.impact: No bug today, but artboards can never wrap to a grid; with many artboards the document becomes an unusably wide horizontal strip. Pure design ceiling / minor dead generality, not incorrectness.

allFindings.title: AABB / align / smart-guides use getBBox(), which excludes stroke width and markers
allFindings.evidence: getElementAABB and collectCandidates rely on (el as SVGGraphicsElement).getBBox() then transformedAABB. getBBox returns the geometry box without stroke/marker extents.
allFindings.impact: Align-left/right/top/bottom and smart-guide edges align geometry centers/edges, not the visible inked edges, so a thick-stroked rect aligned 'left' against a hairline looks ~strokeWidth/2 off. This is a known SVG caveat and matches many editors, but it is a real visible-vs-computed mismatch worth documenting.

allFindings.title: Paste re-IDs only the top element; transferred descendants keep original ids → duplicate ids in document
allFindings.evidence: attrs.id = generateId() (line 76) is applied only to the top element built from `attrs`. The child nodes are then moved verbatim from the parsed clipboard original: `while (original.firstChild) { created.appendChild(original.firstChild) }` (lines 92-94). Those descendants still carry their serialized `id="vf-N"` attributes from copySelection()'s XMLSerializer output.
allFindings.impact: After pasting any element that has children with ids (groups, multi-tspan PDF text, compound shapes), the document contains duplicate ids. doc.getElement(id) uses svg.querySelector('#'+id) (document.ts:88) which silently returns the FIRST match, so later selection-by-id, layer lookups, and graft/export keyed on ids resolve to the wrong element. Duplicate ids also make exported SVG/PDF non-conformant.
allFindings.fix: After transferring children, walk the created subtree and reassign every descendant id via generateId() (and patch any intra-subtree references like clip-path/url(#..), fill=url(#..)). Do this inside the parse step so the AddElementCommand stores already-uniquified attrs.

allFindings.title: GroupCommand undo re-parents children to sel[0]'s parent, not their original parents (cross-layer group corrupts layers)
allFindings.evidence: Constructor captures a single `this.parent` (EditorContext.tsx:96 passes `sel[0].parentElement`). undo() does `for (const child of this.children) { this.parent.insertBefore(child, this.group) }` (lines 246-248) — all children go back into the ONE captured parent. Marquee selection collects children across multiple non-locked visible layers (selectTool.ts:693-713), so a group can legitimately span layers.
allFindings.impact: Group elements from two layers, then undo: every grouped element is dumped into the first element's layer. The other layer silently loses its content; undo does not restore the prior document structure. Data/structure corruption that survives further edits and export.
allFindings.fix: Capture per-child {parent, nextSibling} at construction time and restore each child to its own original parent/position on undo. Or refuse to group a cross-parent selection at the call site.

allFindings.title: GroupCommand uses selection order, not DOM order, for child re-insertion and group placement
allFindings.evidence: `this.insertBefore = children[0]` (line 234) places the group where the FIRST-SELECTED child was, and execute()/undo() iterate children in array order. Shift-click selection is built in click order via toggleSelection (selectTool.ts:495 → selection.ts push), so children[] is click order, not document order.
allFindings.impact: Grouping shift-clicked elements (selected back-to-front) places the group at the wrong z-position and, on undo, re-inserts children in click order — scrambling their original stacking. Wrong visual z-order after group/ungroup round-trips.
allFindings.fix: Sort `children` by their actual DOM position within the common parent before computing insertBefore and before append; capture original nextSibling per child for faithful undo.

allFindings.title: Remove/Cut/Delete leave stale Element refs in selection; no command restores selection on undo/redo
allFindings.evidence: cutSelection calls clearSelection() AFTER history.execute (clipboard.ts:31) — fine — but Delete in EditorContext.tsx:137 also clears. However NO command's undo() touches selection: e.g. RemoveElementCommand.undo (commands.ts:141-148) re-inserts the element but selection stays empty; AddElementCommand.undo removes an element that may still be in the live `active.selected` array (selection.ts holds raw Element refs, never purged on removeElement). updateOverlay() then calls getBBox() on detached nodes (caught) but the ref lingers.
allFindings.impact: Undo of a delete restores geometry but not selection (every keyboard op after undo no-ops until re-click). Worse, deleting via a path that does not clearSelection (e.g. programmatic removeElement, layer clear) leaves detached elements in the selection array, so a subsequent nudge/duplicate/group operates on orphaned nodes — silent no-ops or resurrection of deleted content on duplicate.
allFindings.fix: Make removeElement / RemoveElementCommand.execute purge the element from SelectionState; have undo() restore the prior selection snapshot. Capture-and-restore selection should be a CommandHistory-level concern (snapshot selected ids around execute/undo/redo).
