allFindings.title: AddElementCommand.execute silently drops the element on redo when parent is disconnected
allFindings.evidence: execute() re-add path: `if (this.parent.isConnected) { this.parent.appendChild(this.element) }` (lines 98-100). The else branch is empty — if the parent layer was removed and re-added (a different DOM node) or detached, redo does nothing and the element vanishes with no error.
allFindings.impact: Redo of a paste/add after the target layer was deleted/recreated (e.g. undo layer-delete, which may reconstruct nodes) silently loses the pasted content. Undo/redo stack and DOM diverge.
allFindings.fix: Fall back to the live active layer (doc.getActiveLayer()) or the document model when this.parent is disconnected, or invalidate redo when the anchor parent is gone.

allFindings.title: Keyboard handler only excludes INPUT/TEXTAREA, not contenteditable/SELECT — focus-stealing gap relies entirely on isKeyboardCaptured
allFindings.evidence: `const tag = (e.target as HTMLElement)?.tagName; if (tag === 'INPUT' || tag === 'TEXTAREA') return` (lines 58-59). No check for isContentEditable or SELECT. Ctrl combos are explicitly still processed even under isKeyboardCaptured (line 63: `if (isKeyboardCaptured() && !e.ctrlKey) return`).
allFindings.impact: If any editable surface is a contenteditable div or a focused <select> (PropertiesPanel has several <select>), Ctrl+C/X/V/D/G and Delete fire the canvas handlers instead of the field, and even single-key Delete can leak when capture is off. Matches the documented historical 'inputs swallowing / canvas stealing' fault-line.
allFindings.fix: Replace tagName check with: bail if (e.target as HTMLElement)?.isContentEditable or tag in {INPUT,TEXTAREA,SELECT}. Prefer driving suppression off the focused element rather than the global isKeyboardCaptured flag.

allFindings.title: setActiveDocument swaps state pointers but leaks subscribers bound to the old SelectionState instance
allFindings.evidence: setActiveDocument only reassigns the module `active` pointer (selection.ts:39). React components subscribe via subscribeSelection which pushes into `active.listeners` AT SUBSCRIBE TIME (selection.ts:84-88), capturing the then-active instance's listener array. After a swap, notify() on the new instance won't reach subscribers registered against the old instance, and vice versa.
allFindings.impact: Phase-2 multi-document (the stated future) will have PropertiesPanel/LayersPanel stop updating after a document switch. Not yet exercised (single doc today) but the design is a latent interlock trap directly contradicting the file's own multi-doc promise.
allFindings.fix: Route subscribe/notify through a stable dispatcher keyed off the current active state, or re-bind all listeners on setActiveDocument. Document that subscribers must re-subscribe on swap.

allFindings.title: ReorderElementCommand asserts parentElement non-null and never re-validates on undo
allFindings.evidence: `this.parent = element.parentElement!` (line 196). undo()/execute() insertBefore/appendChild into this.parent with no check that element is still under this.parent or that parent is still connected.
allFindings.impact: If an element is reordered then its layer removed (or it is moved by another op) before undo, the captured parent is stale and undo can insert into a detached/foreign parent. Edge-case structure corruption; low because z-order ops require single non-empty selection and are usually atomic.
allFindings.fix: Re-read element.parentElement at execute()/undo() time, or guard with isConnected and bail if the anchor is gone.

allFindings.title: Layer visibility/lock toggles bypass command history: not undoable, not dirty, but DO affect export
allFindings.evidence: toggleVisibility: `el.style.display = el.style.display === 'none' ? '' : 'none'; refreshLayers()` and toggleLock: `el.setAttribute('data-locked','true')` — neither goes through editor.history.execute(). Meanwhile App.tsx wires `dirty = editor.history.canUndo` and the StatusBar hardcodes a green 'Saved' dot.
allFindings.impact: User hides a layer, exports/saves SVG with style.display:none baked in (fileio/serialize reads the live DOM), but the app shows no dirty dot and 'Saved', and Ctrl+Z will NOT restore the hidden layer. Hidden content silently disappears from exports with no undo and no dirty signal — a data-divergence / lost-work trap.
allFindings.fix: Route visibility and lock toggles through a ModifyAttributeCommand (or a style-modify command) via editor.history.execute() so they are undoable and mark the document dirty consistently with every other edit.

allFindings.title: addLayer repositions the new layer OUTSIDE the AddElementCommand, so redo restores wrong z-order
allFindings.evidence: `const cmd = new AddElementCommand(editor.doc, svg, 'g', {...}); editor.history.execute(cmd); const newLayer = cmd.getElement(); if (newLayer && overlay) svg.insertBefore(newLayer, overlay)`. AddElementCommand.execute() does `doc.addElement(parent, ...)` which appendChild's to the END of svg (after the overlay); the insertBefore(overlay) reposition is applied imperatively and is NOT part of the command. On redo, AddElementCommand.execute() re-appends to svg end (line 99 `this.parent.appendChild(this.element)`), and the insertBefore is never replayed.
allFindings.impact: Undo then redo of 'add layer' leaves the layer above the overlay (wrong stacking / rendered above selection handles), diverging from the post-create state. Z-order corruption across undo/redo.
allFindings.fix: Make the insert position part of the command: add an AddElementCommand variant that takes a beforeSibling, or wrap add+reorder in a CompoundCommand so redo replays both steps.

allFindings.title: Layer list shown in raw DOM/paint order (bottom layer on top); move-up/down arrows are inverted vs z-order
allFindings.evidence: refreshLayers maps `editor.doc.getLayerElements()` (document.ts: `Array.from(svg.querySelectorAll('g[data-layer-name]'))`, i.e. document order) directly with no .reverse(). layers[0] is rendered as the TOP row but is painted FIRST = visually at the BOTTOM. moveLayerUp(idx) inserts the element BEFORE layers[idx-1] (earlier in DOM) = pushes it further DOWN the paint stack.
allFindings.impact: Every design tool (Illustrator/Figma/Sketch) lists the top-most painted layer at the top. Here it is inverted, and the up/down arrows move layers opposite to what the visual list implies. Users will reorder layers the wrong way and mis-stack content.
allFindings.fix: Reverse the array for display (and invert the reorder targets accordingly), or document & flip the arrow semantics. Pick the standard top=front convention.

allFindings.title: theme/atrium.ts is entirely dead code; CSS variables are hand-duplicated in index.css and can drift
allFindings.evidence: grep for `theme/atrium`, `defaultAtrium`, `palettes`, `sodiumVapor` across src (excluding the file itself) returns nothing. The CSS custom properties (--color-panel-solid: oklch(98% 0.005 80) etc.) are defined independently in src/index.css. No code reads atrium.ts to call setProperty.
allFindings.impact: ~70 LOC of palettes plus the 'future theme switcher' claim are non-functional. Editing atrium.ts has zero runtime effect; the duplicated values in index.css will silently diverge from atrium.ts over time, misleading future work.
allFindings.fix: Either drive the CSS variables from defaultAtrium at boot (single source of truth) and actually wire a palette switcher, or delete atrium.ts and drop the misleading comment.

allFindings.title: IconGlyph hardcodes dark ink stroke instead of currentColor; defeats active-tool color and any non-light theme
allFindings.evidence: `const strokeColor = IconTheme.ink` (a fixed `oklch(26% 0.025 145)`), used as `<g stroke={strokeColor}>`. LeftRail sets `color: isActive ? 'var(--color-accent-text)' : 'var(--color-muted)'` on the button but the icon ignores it because it never uses currentColor.
allFindings.impact: Active vs inactive tool icons look identical (no color feedback); icons are always dark-green ink regardless of palette, so on the sodiumVapor dark palette they would be near-invisible. Icon theming is broken.
allFindings.fix: Use stroke="currentColor" (and fill driven by currentColor/CSS var) so icons inherit the button's color and respond to theme.

allFindings.title: deleteLayer index bookkeeping uses stale length and ignores deletes above the active layer
allFindings.evidence: `if (activeLayerIdx >= layers.length - 1) setActiveLayerIdx(Math.max(0, layers.length - 2))`. `layers` is the pre-delete (stale) array, and the condition only handles the case where the active layer was last. Deleting a row ABOVE the active row shifts indices but activeLayerIdx is left unchanged.
allFindings.impact: After deleting a lower-indexed layer, activeLayerIdx points at a different element than the highlighted intent; the active-layer effect then sets the wrong layer as the drawing target, or (if out of range) clears the highlight. New shapes can land on an unexpected layer.
allFindings.fix: Recompute the active index from the post-delete list, ideally by tracking the active layer by element identity rather than positional index.

allFindings.title: LayersPanel uses array index as React key while supporting reorder/delete
allFindings.evidence: `{layers.map((layer, idx) => (... <div key={idx} ...>`. Rows are reordered (moveLayerUp/Down) and removed (deleteLayer), but keyed by position.
allFindings.impact: React reconciles rows by position, not identity, so reorder/delete reuse DOM nodes for different layers. Currently cosmetic (rows are stateless), but it will produce wrong focus/transition/animation behavior the moment any per-row state is added.
allFindings.fix: Key by a stable element identity (e.g. assign/read a stable data-layer-id) instead of idx.

allFindings.title: Inspector bottom panel hardcodes a light background, breaking non-light themes
allFindings.evidence: Bottom Layers/Pages container: `background: 'rgba(255,253,249,0.5)'` — a hardcoded near-white, not a CSS var. (Same class of hardcoding appears in TopBar shadows `rgba(60,40,20,...)` and ArtboardDialog overlay `rgba(20,14,8,0.22)`.)
allFindings.impact: On any dark palette this region renders a white slab over dark text — unreadable. Contradicts the stated theme-switcher intent.
allFindings.fix: Use a themed token (e.g. var(--color-panel) or a dedicated --color-panel-soft) instead of literal rgba.

allFindings.title: Inspector 'Pages' tab is wired to a state value/data-role named 'properties' — mislabeled, confusing seam
allFindings.evidence: The tab labeled 'Pages' has `data-role="inspector-properties-tab"` and sets bottomTab to 'properties'; `{bottomTab === 'properties' && (... 'Multi-page support lands with vectorfeld-4w7.')}`. The InspectorTab union is 'properties' | 'layers' but the UI concept is Layers | Pages.
allFindings.impact: Tests/selectors and future maintainers will conflate the dead 'Pages' stub with a real properties tab. Pure naming debt but a real trap for selector-based tests.
allFindings.fix: Rename the union member and data-role to 'pages' to match the visible label.

allFindings.title: TopBar Split button is a live-looking dead control (onSplit never passed, no disabled affordance)
allFindings.evidence: `<button data-role="split" onClick={onSplit} ...>` rendered with full (non-disabled) styling; App.tsx's <TopBar .../> does not pass onSplit, so onSplit is undefined and the click is a no-op. The prop comment says 'inert in v1'.
allFindings.impact: Clicking Split does nothing with no visual hint that it is disabled — a confusing dead-end. Minor since documented as a stub.
allFindings.fix: Render it disabled (or hidden) when onSplit is undefined, matching the LeftRail 'coming soon' treatment.

allFindings.title: Pervasive cursor: 'default' on interactive buttons — wrong affordance everywhere
allFindings.evidence: Essentially every clickable button/row across LayersPanel, TopBar, StatusBar, LeftRail, ArtboardDialog uses `cursor: 'default'` (e.g. layer row line 209, add-layer line 169, TopBar menu words menuWordStyle, StatusBar chipBtnStyle, ArtboardDialog presetBtnStyle).
allFindings.impact: Interactive controls never show the pointer cursor, so users get no hover affordance distinguishing clickable chrome from static text. Inconsistent with native expectations and harms discoverability.
allFindings.fix: Use cursor: 'pointer' for enabled controls and 'not-allowed'/'default' only for disabled ones.

allFindings.title: ArtboardDialog has no Escape-to-cancel or Enter-to-apply and no focus trap
allFindings.evidence: The modal renders a fixed overlay with Cancel/Apply buttons but registers no keydown handler; there is no onKeyDown for Enter (apply) or Escape (close), and no autofocus/focus trap. (Global keydown handlers in EditorContext/Canvas ignore INPUT, so shortcuts don't leak, but the dialog itself offers no keyboard path.)
allFindings.impact: Keyboard users cannot dismiss or confirm the modal without mousing to the buttons; Escape does nothing. Standard modal affordances are missing.
allFindings.fix: Add Escape->onClose and Enter->handleApply (when an input is focused) and autofocus the width field.
